reason: The cited lines show the handler obtains a Puppeteer page, may launch a browser with merged launch options, and for this case waits for and hovers over a selector, returning a fixed success/error message containing the selector. They do not show arbitrary host code execution, access to or return of non-public data, or delivery of agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination; those could depend on omitted details such as how mergedConfig/args are built or what page is loaded, so those effects are not settled by the cited lines. The returned content shown is just status text based on the caller-provided selector/error, not attacker-controlled page content, so UNTRUSTED is not supported.
